name: Long-eared Bunny
alt: Golden chenille crochet bunny with long ears, a pink nose, and a grey jacket
credit: Original design by Marianna Matvey · Buns toys from Marianna
description: Make a soft, long-eared bunny with this free amigurumi crochet pattern. Work the chenille legs and arms first, join them into the body, then shape the head and add the embroidered expression.
presentation: This is a piece-by-piece amigurumi project with the legs and arms crocheted into the body. The sequence below keeps each component in its own section, so you can check your progress without losing your place.
The supplied styled photograph shows a jacket. Clothing instructions are not included in this bunny pattern.
highlights: Plush chenille texture with long, folded ears
Legs and arms joined as the body is worked
Eye sculpting and embroidery for the finishing details
materials: Wolans Bunny Baby, shade 502: 2 skeins, or equivalent 120 m / 100 g chenille yarn
Semi-cotton thread, such as YarnArt Jeans, for eye sculpting, whites, and eyebrows
Sturdy sewing thread matching the body color
12 mm black screw safety eyes
17 mm × 12 mm pink safety nose
3.5 mm crochet hook
Fiberfill stuffing, tapestry needle, sewing needle, stitch marker, and scissors
Optional fabric/craft glue for the nose and securing thread
abbreviations: Decrease; the source recommends invisible decreases
Repeat the enclosed instructions n times
notes: US crochet terminology. The source groups repeated rounds into numbered steps; the printed step labels and repeat counts are retained below.
Stuff the pieces gradually where directed. Leave the ears unstuffed.
Keep the eye-placement and sculpting references beside you before fastening off the head.

sections.title: Legs · make two
sections.intro: Start at the oval sole and stuff gradually as you work.
rows: Ch 8. Starting in the second ch: 1 inc, 5 sc, 3 sc in the last stitch; along the other side: 4 sc. Place marker. (16)
1 sc, 5 dec, 3 sc, 1 dec, 10 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc. (23)
after: Work 4 shift sc. Fold the top edge flat and crochet through both edges: 1 dec, 5 sc, 1 dec. (7) Place the decreases at the sides. Fasten off and hide the yarn inside. Make the second leg identically.

figures.caption: The shaped legs before joining them to the body.
figures.alt: Two stuffed chenille bunny legs with narrowed tops

sections.title: Arms · make two
sections.intro: Stuff the lower part firmly and the upper part lightly.
after: Work 5 shift sc. Fold flat and crochet across both edges: 1 dec, 3 sc, 1 dec. (5) Fasten off and weave in the end.

sections.title: The little tail
after: Sl st and cut the yarn, leaving a tail for sewing. Leave unstuffed or stuff lightly.

sections.title: Body & joined limbs
sections.intro: The legs are attached over two consecutive rounds. Stuff gradually as the body takes shape.
rows: 3 sc, 7 sc with the first leg (inner side), 14 sc, 7 sc with the second leg (inner side), 11 sc. (42)
3 sc, 7 sc with the first leg (folded edge), 14 sc, 7 sc with the second leg (folded edge), 11 sc. (42)
Work 1 shift sc, move the marker, and continue stuffing gradually.
3 sc, 7 sc over the leg, 1 sc, (1 dec, 1 sc) × 4 for the tummy decreases, 1 sc, 7 sc over the leg, 11 sc. (38)
Attach arms: 3 sc, 5 sc with the first arm, 7 sc, 5 sc with the second arm, 4 sc. (24)
after: Stuff the body firmly. Sl st, cut the yarn, and secure.

figures.caption: Joining the legs into the body as you crochet.
figures.alt: Crochet hook joining a bunny leg to the chenille body

sections.title: Long ears · make two
sections.intro: Use the main plush color. Do not stuff.
after: Flatten the opening and crochet 9 sc across both edges. Fold the base in half lengthwise once more and crochet 4 sc through both layers; the ninth stitch sits along the fold. Fasten off and hide the yarn inside.

figures.caption: The long ear before the final fold at its base.
figures.alt: An unstuffed golden crochet bunny ear

sections.title: Head & eye placement
rows: 13 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 25 sc. (45)
12 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 2 sc, 1 dec, 23 sc. (42)
The 2 sc between decreases in round 13 align directly above the 2 sc in round 12.
Insert between rounds 13 and 14, above the outer decreases of rounds 12–13, approximately 6 sc apart. Stuff the head.
after: Stuff firmly, close the remaining hole, fasten off, and weave in the tail.

sections.title: Facial sculpting & embroidery
sections.intro: Use semi-cotton yarn matching the body, such as YarnArt Jeans, and follow the numbered reference points.
rows: Enter at point 1 at the neck base, exit at 2, re-enter at 3, and exit at 1. Pull tight and knot. Repeat: 1 → 4 → 5 → 1.
Use white thread for the eye whites and black for eyebrows and lashes.
Snap or trim the stem of the pink safety nose and glue it centrally between the eyes.

figures.caption: Source diagram showing the eye-sculpting points.
figures.alt: Bunny head with numbered sculpting points around both eyes

assembly: Sew the head to the body with sturdy matching sewing thread across 3 rounds of stitches. Stitch around 2–3 times so the head is firm.
Sew the tail centrally on the lower back.
Sew the ears to the back of the head, roughly level with the eyebrows and about 4–5 rounds behind them. Sew each base flat in a circle.
closing: Set the finished bunny in front of you and take a moment to adjust the ears and expression. The smallest changes in placement give this long-eared companion its personality.
editorialNotes: Source body and head numbering mixes grouped rounds and step labels; preserved without inventing corrections.
No jacket instructions are present in the supplied source.

name: Sitting Calico Kitten
alt: White, black and golden crochet calico kitten with a red collar
description: This free calico cat crochet pattern creates a sitting kitten with a patchwork coat and a tiny collar. Follow the color changes for the head and body, then use the photo sequence to shape and embroider the face.
presentation: The calico markings are worked directly into the rounds. Keep the color key close and follow the changes in order: MY means mud yellow, W means white, and BL means black.
The source uses an internal neck socket and a wire-supported neck stem to create the pose. Its construction photographs are placed beside the relevant stages below.
highlights: Three-color calico markings worked into the stitches
A shaped neck structure for the sitting pose
Three collar finishes included in the source
materials: Non-elastic cotton thread, approximately 1 mm thick, in mud yellow, white and black
1.5 mm crochet hook
Red, black or blue yarn for the chosen collar
Safety eyes: size printed as 0.5 mm in the supplied source; confirm the intended size before fitting
Fiberfill stuffing, sewing needles, scissors, blocking pins and stitch markers
Fabric glue or hot glue and pink blush makeup powder
Craft wire or pipe cleaners for the neck structure
A miniature bell for the collar
abbreviations: Single crochet / 2 sc in one stitch / invisible single crochet decrease
Back loop only / front loop only
Treble crochet / half treble crochet, as named in the source
Ch 3, sl st into the first chain
Repeat the enclosed sequence n times; brackets show final stitch counts
notes: US crochet terminology. The 12 cm size is based on the source’s 1 mm cotton and 1.5 mm hook.
Color changes are written explicitly as MY, W and BL. Keep the yarn changes in the printed order.
The source includes wire, a bell and attached facial details. Treat those construction choices as part of the supplied design; no child-safety claim is made.

sections.title: Head & internal neck socket
sections.intro: Begin in white. The first section forms the internal neck socket before the head expands.
rows: Do not turn; continue in a spiral: (sc, inc) × 12. [36]
MY: 16 sc, inc; W: sc, inc, 10 sc, inc, sc, inc, 16 sc. [52]
MY: 19 sc; W: 32 sc; MY: sc. [52]
MY: 20 sc; W: 30 sc; MY: 2 sc. [52]
MY: 16 sc, 2 dec; W: dec, 8 sc, 3 dec, 13 sc; MY: 3 sc. [46]
MY: 17 sc, inc, sc; W: 9 sc, inc, 13 sc; MY: 4 sc. [48]
MY: 21 sc; W: 23 sc; MY: 4 sc. [48]
MY: 22 sc; W: 11 sc; BL: 4 sc; W: 7 sc; MY: 4 sc. [48]
MY: (3 sc, dec, 3 sc) × 2, 3 sc, dec, 2 sc; W: 4 sc, dec, 3 sc; BL: 3 sc, dec, sc; W: 5 sc, dec; MY: 3 sc. [42]
MY: 21 sc; W: 6 sc; BL: 7 sc; W: 6 sc; MY: 2 sc. [42] Stuff as you go.
MY: 22 sc; W: 4 sc; BL: 9 sc; W: 6 sc; MY: 1 sc. [42]
MY: (5 sc, dec) × 3, 2 sc; W: 2 sc; BL: sc, dec, 5 sc, dec, sc; W: 4 sc, dec. [36]
MY: 21 sc; W: sc; BL: 10 sc; W: 4 sc. [36]
MY: (2 sc, dec, 2 sc) × 3, 2 sc, dec; BL: 4 sc, dec, 4 sc; W: dec, 2 sc. [30]
MY: (3 sc, dec) × 3, 3 sc; BL: (dec, 3 sc) × 2; W: dec. [24]
MY: (sc, dec, sc) × 3, sc, dec; BL: (2 sc, dec) × 2, sc. [18]
after: Cut and fasten off. Weave through the front loops to close the hole.

figures.caption: The source marks an eight-stitch space for the eyes.
figures.alt: White crochet cat head with pins showing eight stitches between eye positions

rows: Position the safety eyes between R20 and R21, with exactly 8 stitches between them.
Follow the source photo sequence to sculpt around the eyes, then embroider the nose, mouth and whiskers.
Apply soft pink blush to the cheeks and lightly to the nose, as shown in the source photographs.

sections.title: Ears · make two
sections.intro: Make one mud-yellow ear and one black ear.
after: Cut the yarn, leaving a long sewing tail. Flatten the base and sew its two sides together. Pin and sew the ears between R3 and R8, counting down from the top of the head.

figures.caption: The two contrasting ears before attachment.
figures.alt: One black and one golden crochet cat ear

sections.title: Front legs · make two
sections.intro: Use white yarn. Do not stuff these pieces.
after: Cut the yarn and fasten off.

sections.title: Body & joined front legs
sections.intro: Begin in white and stuff as you go. Keep the front legs ready for R18.
rows: (inc, 4 sc) × 2, inc, 5 sc, inc, 12 sc, inc, 6 sc. [41]
MY: inc, 12 sc, inc, 5 sc; W: 3 sc, inc, 8 sc, inc, 2 sc; BL: 7 sc. [45]
BL: sc; MY: 21 sc; W: 15 sc; BL: 8 sc. [45]
BL: 2 sc; MY: 6 sc, inc, 13 sc; W: 14 sc; BL: 9 sc. [46]
BL: 3 sc; MY: 19 sc; W: 15 sc; BL: 9 sc. [46]
BL: 2 sc; MY: 18 sc; W: 19 sc; BL: 7 sc. [46]
BL: sc; MY: 18 sc; W: 22 sc; BL: 5 sc. [46]
MY: 20 sc; W: 2 sc, 2 dec, 2 sc, inc, 4 sc, inc, 2 sc, 2 dec, sc; BL: 5 sc. [44]
MY: 19 sc; W: 22 sc; BL: 3 sc. [44]
MY: 18 sc; W: 8 sc, dec, sc, 2 inc, sc, dec, 10 sc. [44]

MY: 15 sc; BL: 2 sc; W: 10 sc on the body, 10 sc on the first leg, skip 2 stitches on the first leg and 2 on the body; 3 sc; 10 sc on the second leg, skip 2 stitches on the second leg and 2 on the body; 10 sc on the body.
W: 2 sc; MY: 12 sc; BL: 3 sc; W: 46 sc. [60]
W: 3 sc; MY: 2 dec, 2 sc, 2 dec, sc; BL: 5 sc; W: 41 sc. [56]
W: dec, 3 sc; MY: 4 sc, dec; BL: 4 sc; W: 41 sc. [54]
W: dec, 7 sc; BL: dec, 5 sc; W: 7 sc, dec, 4 sc, dec, 3 sc, dec, 4 sc, dec, 12 sc. [48]
W: 4 sc, dec, 3 sc; BL: sc, dec, 4 sc, dec; W: (4 sc, dec) × 5. [40] Stuff as you go.
W: 6 sc, dec, 4 sc; BL: 2 sc, dec, 2 sc; W: 4 sc, dec, (6 sc, dec) × 2. [35]
W: 2 sc, dec, 5 sc, dec, sc; BL: 4 sc, dec; W: (5 sc, dec) × 2, 3 sc. [30]
Insert folded craft wire or pipe cleaners following the source photos, then wrap with thread or yarn.
12 sc for 9 rounds. Stuff firmly around the wire. [12]
after: Cut the yarn and fasten off.

figures.caption: Inside the body before the joined-leg round.
figures.alt: Inside a calico crochet body showing yarn color changes

figures.caption: Source reference for the wrapped neck support.
figures.alt: A wire neck support wrapped with yarn above the crochet body

sections.title: Back legs · make two
rows: W: ch 5. Starting in the second ch, sc, 2 inc, 3 sc in the same stitch; along the opposite side: 2 sc, inc. [12]
after: Stuff lightly. Leave a long tail for sewing. Sew onto R7 and R8 of the body, leaving 5–6 stitches between the back legs. Sew the inner sides of the front legs together, following the source photos.

figures.caption: The seated leg arrangement.
figures.alt: Crochet kitten’s front and back paws positioned for a seated pose

sections.title: Patchwork tail
rows: BL: sc, dec, sc; MY: 4 sc. [7]
after: Leave a long sewing tail and attach to R8–R9 at the back of the body.

sections.title: Choose a collar finish
rows: In black or red: ch 27 and join to the first chain with sl st to make a ring. Work 11 sc, 2 hdc, (dc, picot, dc) into the same stitch, 2 hdc, 11 sc. Fasten off and attach a miniature bell at the point.
In blue: ch 25 and join the ends to form a ring. Work (5 sc, picot) × 5. Fasten off and attach the bell to one picot.
In red: ch 27 and join to the first chain. 27 sc. [27]
(Ch 3, sl st) × 27 across. Fasten off and attach the bell centrally.

assembly: Check the source eye placement, ear positioning, and seated leg arrangement before securing all parts.
Attach the back legs and tail at the round positions given above.
Fit the chosen collar and weave in remaining ends. Preserve the designer credit when sharing finished work.
closing: The calico colors do much of the storytelling here. Finish by checking the face and sitting posture together, then settle your little kitten somewhere its expression can be enjoyed.
editorialNotes: Designer’s personal-use and attribution notice retained in the source record. Public redistribution permission is not established by this local import.
The source prints safety eyes as 0.5 mm and has stitch-count inconsistencies; no unconfirmed corrections have been substituted.

name: Pumpkin Cat
alt: Black crochet cat wearing a purple witch hat on an orange pumpkin
credit: Original illustrated pattern by Massiel Martinez · @MASSIMARTZ_ · Supplied Crovely English edition
description: Bring a little Halloween character to your shelf with this free pumpkin cat crochet pattern. The project pairs a small black cat with a purple witch hat, an orange pumpkin, and a leafy finishing detail.
presentation: This project brings together several small components, so the instructions are arranged by piece with a separate finishing section. Keep the two cat hooks and pumpkin hook labeled as you work.
The rich purple, orange and green details are the little touches that give the finished display its autumn character.
highlights: A sculpted pumpkin with an eight-lobed leaf cap
A pointed witch hat with openings for the ears
materials: Cotton yarn approximately 2 mm thick
Black, orange, purple, dark green, light green and pink yarn, plus a little white yarn or embroidery thread
2.00 mm hook for the cat pieces
2.20 mm hook for the hat and band
2.25 mm hook for the pumpkin and leaves
7 mm safety eyes, stuffing, yarn needle, scissors and pins
Craft glue; optional wire for the tail and buckle
abbreviations: Single crochet / half double crochet / double crochet
2 sc in one stitch / single crochet 2 stitches together
Back loop only / front loop only
Repeat the bracketed sequence n times; final counts are in parentheses
notes: US crochet terms. Finished height is approximately 12 cm using the source materials.
Use 2.00 mm for the cat, 2.20 mm for the hat and band, and 2.25 mm for the pumpkin and leaves.
The source describes wire, glued parts and small eyes as a decorative construction. Its construction choices have been retained.

sections.title: Hello, little kitty · head
sections.intro: Black yarn · 2.00 mm hook.
rows: Insert between Rnds 12 and 13, with 5 stitches between them.
after: Fasten off, leaving a long sewing tail.

figures.caption: The small black head before assembly. Original illustrated reference; embedded labels are in Spanish.
figures.alt: Illustrated source reference for hello, little kitty · head, with photographs of the crochet pieces

sections.title: Tiny paws & happy tail
sections.intro: Black yarn · 2.00 mm hook.
rows: Join the opening with 3 sc. Sew between Rnds 14 and 15 of the body.
Fasten off with a long sewing tail. If using wire, fit it to the tail length and turn the ends inward. Sew between Rnds 5 and 6 of the body.

sections.title: Ears & little muzzle
sections.intro: Black yarn · 2.00 mm hook.
rows: Leave long sewing tails. Attach each ear between Rnds 4 and 8 of the head.
Ch 2. Into the second ch: 2 dc, ch 2, sl st into the same starting chain.
Ch 2, work 2 dc into that same starting chain, ch 2, and sl st into the same chain.
Fasten off and thread the tail onto a yarn needle. Glue the piece between Rnds 14 and 15 of the head.

sections.title: A face to fall for
rows: Indent the eye areas with black yarn, following the source photographs.
Embroider the highlight line in white.
Embroider a small pink nose over the black muzzle.
Pin the head in place and sew it to the body.

figures.caption: Eye-shaping reference from the supplied pattern. Original illustrated reference; embedded labels are in Spanish.
figures.alt: Illustrated source reference for a face to fall for, with photographs of the crochet pieces

sections.title: Pumpkin time
sections.intro: Orange yarn · 2.25 mm hook.
rows: 2 sc, inc, [1 sc BLO, 3 sc, inc] × 7, 1 sc BLO, sc. (48)
4 sc, 1 sc BLO, [5 sc, 1 sc BLO] × 7, sc. Repeat for 10 rounds. (48)
after: Fasten off, leaving a sufficiently long tail for shaping.

figures.caption: The orange pumpkin before its final shaping. Original illustrated reference; embedded labels are in Spanish.
figures.alt: Illustrated source reference for pumpkin time, with photographs of the crochet pieces

sections.title: Shape the pumpkin & add its leaves
sections.intro: Green yarn · 2.25 mm hook.
rows: Pass the yarn along the divisions formed by the back-loop stitches. Repeat the shaping step twice, following the source photographs.
8 sc in MR; join with a sl st. (8)
Ch 6. Starting in the second ch: sc, then hdc in each of the next 4 chains. Sl st into the next stitch of the center ring.
Make 8 lobes. Fasten off and position centrally on the pumpkin with the reverse side facing outward.

sections.title: A hat full of charm
sections.intro: Purple yarn · 2.20 mm hook. The two chain openings accommodate the ears.
rows: 2 sc, inc, 4 sc, inc, ch 10, skip 4 sts, 7 sc, ch 10, skip 4 sts, 7 sc. (44 including chains)
Sc in every stitch and each chain around. (44)
inc, 5 sc, inc, 2 sc, inc, 11 sc, inc, [2 sc, inc] × 2, 10 sc, inc, 5 sc. (52)
after: Fasten off and weave in the end.

sections.title: Hat band & buckle
sections.intro: Orange yarn · 2.20 mm hook.
rows: Ch 22. Starting in the second ch, work 21 sc. Fasten off, weave in the end, and fit around the hat cone.
Form a small rectangle from black wire and glue to the center front of the band.
Pass the ears through the openings and settle the brim around the head.

assembly: Check the source attachment positions for the legs, tail, ears and head.
Position the green leaf cap on the pumpkin with the reverse side outward.
Pin the cat centrally on the leaf cap and pumpkin, check the balance, then sew or glue it in place.
closing: The hat and pumpkin turn this little cat into a miniature autumn display. Let the finishing details settle into place, then give your pumpkin companion a spot on a shelf or desk.
editorialNotes: The supplied PDF does not contain separate cat body rounds. Only the supplied sections are presented; no body instructions have been invented.
Printed hat and pumpkin counts are retained as supplied, without independent pattern testing.

name: Luna the Witchy Cat
alt: Grey crochet witch cat with a mauve pointed hat, ruffled skirt and plum cloak
credit: Pattern and design by Chloe · EMI Creations · @e.m.i_creations
description: Make Luna, a grey witch cat with a pointed hat, wavy skirt, and plum cloak, with this free crochet pattern. This intermediate amigurumi project brings together shaped cat pieces, small clothing details, and facial embroidery.
presentation: Make the head, ears and arms before moving on to the joined body. The cuffs, skirt and hat brim are worked into reserved front loops, giving the outfit its layered finish.
A separate cloak and optional shaped tail complete the character. Keep the finished pieces together until you are ready to pin and sew the final arrangement.
highlights: An intermediate project in US crochet terminology
Layered sleeve cuffs, ruffled skirt and hat brim
A removable-looking cloak tied with crocheted strands
materials: 2.5 mm crochet hook
7 mm safety eyes
4 Seasons Flinders Cotton 8ply, 50 g: less than one ball each of vintage pink, dark grey, light purple, dark purple and black
Fiberfill or toy stuffing
Black DMC stranded thread
Stitch markers and embroidery needles
Optional wire for the tail
abbreviations: Front loop only / back loop only
notes: The source specifies intermediate skill level and American terminology.
Work in continuous rounds unless the instructions say otherwise. Luna measures approximately 13.5 cm with the listed materials.
The sleeve cuff uses light purple in the written instructions. The source’s accompanying caption mentions red; the written color direction is retained here.

sections.title: Head
sections.intro: Dark grey yarn · continuous rounds.
rows: Insert between rounds 15 and 16, 5 stitches apart. Start stuffing the head.
after: Fasten off with a long tail. Weave through the front loops and pull tightly to close the hole; weave in loose ends.

figures.caption: The shaped grey head, before the face is finished.
figures.alt: Stuffed grey crochet cat head held in one hand

sections.title: Ears · make two
sections.intro: Dark grey yarn · do not stuff.
after: Fasten off, leaving a long tail for sewing.

sections.title: Arms & sleeve cuffs · make two
sections.intro: Start with dark grey yarn. The cuffs use light purple.
rows: Do not stuff. Fold the opening and work 4 sc through both loops to close. Fasten off and weave in loose ends.
With the hand facing you, join light purple to a front loop of round 6.
Ch 1; starting in the second stitch from the hook, 9 sc. Sl st in the first stitch of the round. [9]
after: Fasten off and weave in loose ends.

figures.caption: The two-color sleeve before the cuff is added.
figures.alt: A small crochet arm with a dark grey paw and mauve sleeve

sections.title: Body & joined arms
sections.intro: Start in dark grey, then change to light purple.
rows: 5 sc, join the first arm with 4 sc through both loops of the arm and body, 11 sc, join the second arm with 4 sc through both loops, 6 sc. [30]
after: Stuff the body, fasten off and leave a long sewing tail.

figures.caption: The body before the ruffled skirt is finished.
figures.alt: Grey and mauve crochet cat body showing the color-change line

sections.title: The wavy skirt
sections.intro: Light purple yarn. With the body base facing away from you, join into a front loop of round 13.
rows: FLO: ch 1, begin in the second stitch from the hook, 42 hdc-inc. Sl st in the first stitch. [84]
Ch 1, begin in the second stitch from the hook, (hdc, hdc-inc) × 42. Sl st in the first stitch. [126]
after: Fasten off, weave in loose ends and shape the skirt into waves.

figures.caption: The ruffled skirt after both increase rounds.
figures.alt: Mauve ruffled crochet skirt around a grey cat body

sections.title: Feet & pink pads · make two
sections.intro: Dark grey feet with vintage pink pads.
rows: Stuff lightly. Fasten off and leave a long tail. Weave through the front loops and pull tightly to close; keep the tail for sewing.
Vintage pink: MR, 6 sc. [6] Close with an invisible sl st and leave a long sewing tail.

sections.title: The little cloak
sections.intro: Dark purple yarn · work in rows. Ch 25 and begin in the second chain from the hook.
rows: dec, 20 sc, dec, ch 1 and turn. [22]
dec, 18 sc, dec, ch 1 and turn. [20]
Work sc around the next 3 edges, with 3 sc at each corner. Close with an invisible sl st. Fasten off and weave in loose ends.
At row 5 on each side, join dark purple yarn and ch 30. Fasten off and trim the tail to 5 mm, as directed in the source.

figures.caption: The cloak after its edging and ties.
figures.alt: Deep plum crochet cloak with two chain ties

sections.title: The curved tail
sections.intro: Dark grey yarn · do not stuff.
after: Fasten off with a long sewing tail. Optionally insert wire and shape it into an S, as described in the source.

sections.title: The pointed hat
sections.intro: Start in light purple and work in rounds.
rows: Sl st to close. Change to light purple.
FLO: ch 1, start in the second stitch from the hook, (2 sc, inc) × 12. Sl st in the first stitch. [48]
Ch 1, start in the second stitch from the hook, (7 sc, inc) × 6. Sl st in the first stitch. [54]
Ch 1, start in the second stitch from the hook, (4 sc, inc, 4 sc) × 6. Sl st in the first stitch. [60]
after: Fasten off and weave in loose ends.

figures.caption: The completed pointed hat and brim.
figures.alt: Mauve pointed crochet witch hat with a contrasting band

assembly: Embroider black whiskers on either side of the head between rounds 14 and 17, 2 stitches from the eyes.
With black DMC thread, embroider the nose between the eyes at rounds 15–16. Add vintage-pink cheek lines at rounds 16–17, 1 stitch from the eyes.
Sew the ears to the head between rounds 4 and 10, then sew the head to the body.
Sew the pink pads to the feet between rounds 5 and 7. Embroider three evenly spaced pink toe lines between rounds 1 and 3.
Sew the feet to the front of the body between rounds 7 and 13, 4 stitches apart.
Sew the tail at the back between rounds 5 and 7. Put on the cloak and hat, then weave in remaining ends.
closing: With her soft colors and layered outfit, Luna works beautifully as a small seasonal display. Finish by arranging the cloak and hat, then check that each sewn detail sits just where you want it.
